source: NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch. 9 (Atmospheric Circulation and Weather Systems).

sections.heading: 1. Atmospheric Pressure and Winds
points: **Atmospheric pressure** = weight of air; decreases with altitude; measured in **millibars (barometer)**.
Wind blows from **high to low pressure**; its direction is modified by the **Coriolis force** (deflects right in Northern Hemisphere, left in Southern — **Ferrel's Law**) and friction.
The **pressure gradient force** drives winds; **isobars** = lines of equal pressure.

sections.heading: 2. Pressure Belts and Planetary Winds
points: Seven pressure belts: **Equatorial low, two Subtropical highs, two Subpolar lows, two Polar highs**.

sub: **Trade winds** — from subtropical high to equatorial low (NE in N. Hemisphere, SE in S).
**Westerlies** — from subtropical high toward subpolar low.
**Polar easterlies** — from polar high to subpolar low.

points: **Seasonal winds** = **monsoons** (reverse with season); **local winds** (loo, land/sea breeze, mountain/valley breeze, Chinook, Foehn).

sections.heading: 3. Air Masses and Fronts
points: **Air mass** = a large body of air with uniform temperature and humidity (source regions).
**Front** = boundary between two different air masses — **warm, cold, stationary, occluded fronts**.
Fronts bring changes in weather (clouds, precipitation).

sections.heading: 4. Cyclones
points: **Tropical cyclones** — form over warm tropical oceans (>27°C); intense low pressure with a calm **'eye'**; called **hurricanes, typhoons, cyclones** in different regions; very destructive (storm surge).
**Temperate (extra-tropical) cyclones** — form along fronts in mid-latitudes; larger, less violent, bring widespread rain.
**Anticyclones** = high pressure, clear calm weather.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Wind blows high → low pressure; Coriolis deflects right (N) / left (S) — Ferrel's Law.
Seven pressure belts; planetary winds: trades, westerlies, polar easterlies.
Trade winds: NE (N. Hemisphere), SE (S. Hemisphere).
Tropical cyclone needs warm ocean (>27°C); has a calm 'eye'.
Temperate cyclones form along fronts (mid-latitudes).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Coriolis force deflects winds right in the Northern Hemisphere, left in the Southern** (Ferrel's Law).
**Trade winds blow from subtropical high toward the equatorial low**.
**Tropical cyclones need warm seas (>27°C)**; they weaken over land.
The calm centre of a tropical cyclone is the **'eye'**.
